chunks: And from him, from Muhammad, from his uncle, who said: And Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated to me from Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal al-Khuza'i from Uthman ibn Sa'id from a man from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He said: 'Indeed, near Kufah is a grave; whoever afflicted by distress visits it and prays two or four rak'at at it, Allah will relieve his distress and fulfill his need.'
I asked: Is it the grave of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him)? He said to me with a nod of his head: 'No.'
I said: Then is it the grave of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him)? He said to me with a nod of his head: 'Yes.'

key_terms.بِرَأْسِهِ: with a nod of his head
key_terms.مَكْرُوبٌ: one afflicted by distress or anxiety

ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of praying at the grave of Imam Ali in Kufah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* specifically identifies the grave of Imam Ali (AS) in Kufah as a locus of divine relief (*kashf al-kurba*), distinguishing it from the grave of Imam Husayn (AS) through the Imam’s affirmative nod. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the intercessory and spiritual efficacy of visiting the Ahl al-Bayt, particularly in Kufah, where Imam Ali’s final resting place serves as a conduit for resolving worldly and spiritual distress.
